chunks: He said: And Abdullah ibn Jamil narrated to me from Salih ibn Abi Saeed al-Qummat, who said: And Abdullah ibn Ghalib narrated to me, saying: I recited this poem to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

"If you are indeed the one hoped for for what we see, then that is the one from the Exalted [God] for whom we seek [blessings]." He said: "Not I am the possessor of this quality, but this one is its possessor," and he pointed with his hand to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: Who did Imam al-Sadiq point to as the possessor of the high status mentioned in the poem?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) redirects the poetic praise of high status from himself to his son, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.), serving as a clear textual proof for the Imamate of the latter. This specific designation is crucial in refuting the Waqifiya, a sect that halted their belief in the Imamate at Imam al-Sadiq, by demonstrating the continuous line of authority. The gesture underscores the theological concept of *Nass* (designation) in Shia jurisprudence, affirming the transition of spiritual and political leadership.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 36 - Narrated to me Abdullah bin Jamil from Salih bin Abi Saeed Qummat from Abdullah bin Ghalib that: I composed and recited the following Qasida to Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s):
“If you had only been our source of hope as I can see. It is about which we request Almighty Allah for you.” “Not I, but he has these qualities,” he said pointing to his son, Musa.
